scope: v2: recommendation consistency + tone + sample-vs-total + hedged-vs-asserted

findings.message: The 'About This Report' section opens in first-person plural ('We audited', 'We fetch', 'We then review') but the Findings priority blocks switch inconsistently: Priority 3 opens with 'We identified' (first-person) while Priority 7 opens with 'We score' and Priority 8 opens with 'We record' — these are consistent — however the 'Summary of Findings' closing paragraph switches back to first-person ('We invite the team') after the structured Findings section uses first-person throughout, which is internally consistent. The real tone-inconsistency is in the 'Structured Data Inventory' section, which mixes third-person passive ('No Schema.org JSON-LD entities were detected') with first-person ('the 7 pages we audited') within the same short paragraph.
findings.context: No Schema.org JSON-LD entities were detected across the audited set. Adding at least one typed entity per page...a wider audit identifies the same gaps across the rest of the estate.

findings.message: The 'Structured Data Inventory' section asserts 'a wider audit identifies the same gaps across the rest of the estate' — treating a 7-page sample finding (zero schema markup) as though it has already been confirmed across the full site, which has not been audited.
findings.context: a wider audit identifies the same gaps across the rest of the estate.

findings.message: The 'Cross-Page Consistency' table reports 'Skip link: 0% — 7 pages missing it', but the Marker Reachability table directly above records 'Skip link (accessibility): Yes | Yes | Body | Yes | No', asserting a skip link is present — these two statements cannot both be true for the same audited pages, and the consistency table implies a site-wide 0% conclusion from a contradicted sample finding.

The 'llms-full.txt' section hedges whether publishing the file 'would be worthwhile' by saying it 'depends on the content depth of the full site, which our audited sample of 7 pages does not yet measure' — but the absence of the file is a binary, deterministic fact (404 confirmed), and the recommendation to publish it appears without hedging in Priority 7; the inconsistency in confidence between the Discovery Files section (hedged) and the Findings section (asserted) is a material imbalance for the same item.
findings.context: Whether adding it would be worthwhile depends on the content depth of the full site, which our audited sample of 7 pages does not yet measure
